what: Sleep is maintenance, and it is one of the two clock users (Akien 2026-09-30: "we did put sleep on the clock. and sleep was to be maintenance tasks."). Its trigger is not an hour of the day (Akien 2026-08-06, ideas/2026-08-06-the-sleep-trigger-captured-across-three-turns.json: "it's about when other external things won't trouble it" — "a '3 hours without a human' screensaver like trigger"). Sleep is a peer handoff and the cairn device is its manager (Akien 2026-09-30): on the ground loop's spawned pulse the cairn device checks the trigger, and when it has tripped it mints; the cairn device then hands one token round the roster, one device at a time, and each device's SHIM does that device's maintenance and answers. token.py: roster() (alpha-sorted ids of devices whose shim answers the `sleep` verb), mint(), receive_answer() (stale or out-of-turn answers refused loudly), standing(). The cairn device fronts it with verbs sleep-token (a device's answer) and sleep-cycle (mint | show).
why: One token rotation replaces N sleep daemons, serial by design (measured OOM history n=3). The shape is a hub: cairn hands to one device at a time and every device answers cairn. The announce feed is the RECORD of the rotation, never its transport.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.sleep_cycle import token`; `token.mint(bus, ...)`, `token.receive_answer(bus, body, ...)`, `token.standing()`, `token.roster()`. Over the bus: verb `sleep-cycle` to cairn with {"act": "mint"|"show"}; a device's shim answers with verb `sleep-token`.
entry: Fresh design under ticket bf146e9e3967; composes bus.post and the cairn device's verbs — nothing grafted.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter once a voyage freezes here (Law 5). Runtime state is instance-space only: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/sleep_cycle/cycle.json (the standing cycle) and superseded.jsonl (open cycles a later mint replaced).
filed_edges: (a) the roster is still read from probes/ folders holding sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py — a probe fired on nothing; it moves to devices whose shim answers `sleep` (the cleanup ticket).
(b) the clock entry that mints a cycle — the ground loop's sleep entry, spawned (ground loop charter filed edge (c)); replaces the idle-trigger ticket 9b6b392ebcfe.
(c) a device that never answers holds the token forever — a stalled cycle is visible in standing() but not yet loud.
gates: proof gate (tester) — proofs/test_token_rotation.py on BusDevice.scratch: order, single holder, n+1 announce records, close once, stale id refused, empty roster closes; durability gate — git commit.
falsifier: RED on any of: a token that stops at a device that answered; two devices holding an unanswered token at once; a complete rotation over n devices leaving other than n+1 announce records for its cycle_id; a stale or out-of-turn answer accepted; a cycle closing twice or never; an empty roster that does not close at mint.
how_it_learns: It does not. The rotation is a mechanism; what is learned from the answers each device returns is the parent ticket's question (4de7baf7e255), read off the announce feed and cycle.json.
traces_to: Law 5 (the standing cycle is instance state; the record is the feed)
Law 6 (each device does its own work in its own probe; cairn only hands)
Law 7 (a stale or out-of-turn answer is refused on the record, never dropped)
Law 8 (the proof drives the rotation over fixture devices a hollow build could not satisfy)
owner: CC owns the code + proofs and gates writes to them; Akien owns the design (the hub shape, the opt-in roster).
